name: Single-Arm Triceps Pushdown

confidenceKey.measured: a study measured it (goniometer, motion capture or EMG)
confidenceKey.documented: a guideline, manual or manufacturer states it
confidenceKey.range, coach consensus: coaching sources agree; no measured number
confidenceKey.derived: worked out from geometry or from the sources above; not measured directly
confidenceKey.unverified: no source found; do not present as fact

angleConventions: Elbow flexion 0 deg = arm straight. Shoulder flexion 0 deg = upper arm hanging vertical beside the trunk. Torso lean 0 deg = trunk vertical.

appData.siblingExercises: The library also has lib_triceps_pushdown, lib_rope_triceps_pushdown and lib_straight_bar_triceps_pushdown, all on the same high-pulley station, so one cable-station asset can serve all four with different attachments.

keep: Single D-handle at the high pulley, one hand.
Elbow pinned at the side, upper arm still (ACE).
Elbow drift forward and leaning into the weight as the two main mistakes.

flags.finding: Now measured: two studies of the unilateral cable pushdown used a 90 to 0 deg elbow range set by goniometer (Villalba 2024; Maeo 2023). Keep 90 deg as the start, with sources.

flags.item: peakAt 0.35 'highest approaching the near-extended bottom', sourced to a fitnessprogramer instruction.
flags.finding: The quoted line only says to extend fully; it says nothing about when effort peaks. No EMG-by-angle data for the pushdown was found. Geometry points the other way: with the cable running close to vertical, the cable's lever arm about the elbow is longest near 90 deg and shrinks toward lockout. Treat the peak as unverified; do not ship the old value.

flags.item: Grip was not specified (palm down vs palm up).
flags.finding: Sources split: fitnessprogramer, GettFit and Jefit use overhand; ExRx's one-arm pushdown uses underhand. Villalba 2024 tested both on this exact exercise. Default chosen below with reasons.

modelThis.station: A selectorized dual adjustable pulley (functional trainer): two tall columns, each with a weight stack and a pulley carriage that slides on a vertical track and locks with a pop-pin; a swivelling pulley head on each carriage; joined at the top by a frame. Use one column, carriage locked at its highest position.
modelThis.attachment: One single D-handle (stirrup): steel D-ring at the top, two straps or side plates down to a rotating, knurled cylindrical grip.
modelThis.why: Villalba 2024 ran this exact exercise on a dual adjustable pulley cable station. The same asset serves every cable exercise in the library at any height, and ACE only requires the attachment to be above head height. Life Fitness ships its dual pulley with a triceps rope, short and long strap handles, so the other three pushdowns reuse the station.
modelThis.confidence: documented (machine type used in the study); choice of product is a design decision

parts.detail: selectorized plates on two guide rods, pin selector; top plate with a selector stem
pulley carriage moves up and down the column and locks at set holes: 22 positions on Life Fitness Signature DAP (retailer spec), 17 on Matrix Aura G3-MS24 (retailer summary)
Matrix G3-MS24 parts list: pulleys of 115 mm and 90 mm diameter
Matrix G3-MS24 2:1 (91 kg stack = 45 kg at the handle); Life Fitness Signature DAP 4:1 (retailer: 2 x 177 kg stacks, 97.5 lb effective per side)
parts.confidence: documented (retailer); one retailer lists LF stacks as 2 x 195 lb, a conflict

parts.detail: Rogue Single Handle: 8.5 in (216 mm) from top of D-ring to centre of grip; grip 5 in (127 mm) wide; 25 mm steel grip (28.5, 32, 45 mm aluminium options); grip spins on a shoulder bolt; 1.5 in nylon webbing. Other makers: 22 mm x 136 mm (K-Sport), 25 mm x 152 mm (Bells of Steel), 25 mm x 100 mm (Fringe).

lifeFitnessSignatureDAP.value: 113 x 156 x 240 cm (L x W x H)
lifeFitnessSignatureDAP.confidence: documented (retailer); another retailer lists 44 x 62 x 95 in

matrixAuraG3MS24.value: single adjustable pulley column, 68 x 70 x 240 cm, 91 kg stack, max user 136 kg

matrixAuraG3MS53.value: dedicated triceps pressdown station (fixed high pulley), 85 x 59 x 240 cm, 91 kg stack

topPulleyHeight.value: frames are about 240 cm tall; the exact height of the pulley at the top carriage position was not found

equipment.variantsNotModelled: Cable crossover (two towers further apart), single adjustable column (Matrix G3-MS24), and dedicated fixed-pulley pressdown stations (Matrix G3-MS53). Strap handles (Life Fitness ships these) look different from a steel D-handle.
equipment.recommendation: If one manufacturer-documented geometry is needed for exact modelling, use the Matrix Aura owner's guide figures (column 68 x 70 x 240 cm, pulleys 115/90 mm) and the Rogue Single Handle dimensions; both come from the maker.

setup.text: Clip a single D-handle to the cable.
Move the pulley carriage to its highest setting.
Stand facing the machine, feet hip-width or in a staggered (walking) stance, knees slightly bent.
Take the handle in one hand, palm down, with a full grip: thumb wrapped round the handle.
Stand close enough that the cable is taut with the elbow at 90 deg, so there is load at the top of the rep.
setup.landmark: the weight lifts off the stack at the start position

setup.text: Set the working upper arm vertical with the elbow at the side, elbow bent to 90 deg and pointing down.
setup.landmark: elbow in line with the mid-point of the trunk

setup.text: Brace the abs with a natural low-back arch; pull the shoulder blades back and down.
Free hand on the hip or lightly on the machine frame.

torso_spine.value: upright to slightly forward: 0-10 deg lean from the hips, spine neutral with its natural low-back curve, braced
torso_spine.confidence: range, coach consensus (Villalba: 'spine in anatomical position'; Hussain: 'torso slightly leaned forward'; one coach site gives about 10 deg)

shoulder.value: 0 deg flexion and 0 deg abduction: upper arm vertical, elbow at the side; neutral rotation

forearm.value: pronated (palm down) for the default model; forearm horizontal

hips.value: extended, or a slight hinge if leaning

freeArm.value: hand on hip or on the frame

cableLine.value: from the top pulley down to the handle, close to vertical and in front of the working arm

shoulder.value: unchanged: upper arm vertical, elbow at the side

elbow.value: 0 deg: fully straight without a forceful lock; brief pause
elbow.confidence: measured (90 to 0 deg); ACE adds 'do not lock out'

hand.value: beside the front of the upper thigh

shoulder.value: 0 deg; upper arm has not moved

wrist.value: neutral; knuckles in line with the forearm

torso.value: same lean as the start; no extra hinge

defaultChoice.value: pronated (palm down) on a single D-handle
defaultChoice.why: Most how-to sources for this exercise use it (fitnessprogramer, GettFit, Jefit), and it is the PRON-H condition of the only study of this exact exercise. The palm-up version is a valid variant.

width.value: one hand, in line with the working shoulder

handleInPalm.value: grip across the palm inside the D-ring; the frame or straps rise from both ends of the grip to the ring above the back of the hand
handleInPalm.confidence: documented (handle shape); exact spot in the palm unverified

wristStack.value: wrist straight, not bent back under the load

fingers.value: four fingers round the grip, thumb wrapped over

variants.name: supinated (palm up)
variants.detail: ExRx's one-arm pushdown uses it. Villalba 2024: higher long-head EMG than palm down (effect size 0.53), more wrist-extensor activity, and fewer reps at the same load.

variants.name: neutral (palm in) with a D-handle or single rope
variants.detail: Listed as an option ('palm facing in or down').

rom.value: elbow from 90 deg to 0 deg; ExRx goes deeper on the way up ('until forearm is close to upper arm'), letting the elbow rise a few inches
rom.confidence: measured (90-0); deeper range is a documented variant

tempo.value: 2 s down (extending), brief pause, 2 s up (returning)
tempo.confidence: measured (Villalba metronome 2 s : 2 s; Maeo 2 s : 2 s per a summary)

sides.value: finish one arm, then the other

secondary.note: Wrist flexors (flexor carpi radialis) were most active palm-down, wrist extensors palm-up: the forearm holds the wrist straight against the cable.

stabilizers.note: Lats, teres major and rear delts hold the upper arm against the cable's forward pull (ExRx, summary). ACE asks for an abdominal brace.
stabilizers.confidence: documented (ExRx read as a summary only)

headsNote.value: In pushdowns the long head showed more EMG than the lateral head (ACE study: rope 81 vs 67, bar 75 vs 59, as % of triangle push-up). Villalba found only the long head changed with grip.

peakEffort.value: not measured by angle in any source found
peakEffort.confidence: unverified (geometry suggests the cable's lever arm is longest near 90 deg)

disagreementWithExercisesJson.proposal: Keep primary triceps and secondary forearms. Optionally add stabilizers lats, rear_delts, core.
disagreementWithExercisesJson.why: Forearm activity is measured (Villalba). The stabilizer roles come from ExRx (summary) and ACE's brace cue, not EMG.

mistakes.name: Elbow drifting forward
mistakes.looksLike: On the way up the upper arm swings forward (shoulder flexes) and the elbow leaves the side; on the way down the arm pulls back like a straight-arm pulldown.
mistakes.whyItMatters: Recruits the lats and takes emphasis off the triceps.
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow pinned at the side; let only the forearm move.

mistakes.name: Leaning over the handle
mistakes.looksLike: The trunk hinges well forward and the shoulder rolls over the handle at the bottom, so body weight helps push it down; often with a knee dip.
mistakes.whyItMatters: Body weight and leg drive replace triceps work; a sign the load is too heavy.
mistakes.fix: Lighter load; keep the same slight lean from first rep to last.

mistakes.name: Elbow flaring out
mistakes.looksLike: The elbow drifts away from the ribs to the side (shoulder abducts) as the handle comes down.
mistakes.whyItMatters: Listed beside forward drift as a form fault: the upper arm should stay still so only the elbow moves.
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow tucked against the side.

mistakes.name: Bending the wrist
mistakes.looksLike: The wrist bends back (extends) under a palm-down handle, or curls, so the knuckles are no longer in line with the forearm.
mistakes.whyItMatters: ACE asks for a neutral wrist; the forearm muscles are already working to hold it straight against the handle (Villalba EMG).
mistakes.fix: Keep the wrist straight; lighten the load if it bends.

mistakes.name: Cutting the range
mistakes.looksLike: Reps stop short of a straight arm at the bottom, or turn around well below 90 deg at the top.
mistakes.whyItMatters: Leaves out part of the range the triceps should work through.
mistakes.fix: Straighten fully at the bottom and return to about 90 deg each rep.

keyFacts.text: In the same people over 12 weeks, overhead cable extensions grew the triceps 1.4 times more than pushdowns (+19.9% vs +13.9%), with lighter weights. Pushdowns still built muscle; pairing them with an overhead move covers the long head.
Palm up vs palm down on this exact exercise: palm up gave more long-head activity but fewer reps at the same load; palm down worked the wrist flexors harder.
The number on the stack is not the load at the handle: many dual-pulley stations run 2:1 or 4:1, so a 91 kg stack can be 45 kg at the handle. Weights don't transfer between machines.
Rope pushdowns scored 74% and bar pushdowns 67% of the triceps activity of a triangle push-up; the long head outworked the lateral head in both.

openQuestions: Default grip: palm down chosen (most how-to sources; study condition PRON-H). Palm up is valid and ExRx uses it. Owner may choose.
Single-arm vs two-arm for Version 1 was asked of the owner in docs/FORM-GUIDE-PRODUCTION.md 10.6; this file assumes single-arm as the id says.
Exact torso lean in degrees is not measured anywhere found; 0-10 deg is a coach range.
Where to stand side-to-side relative to the pulley (cable in line with the working shoulder or centred on the body) is not stated by any source found.
Free-hand placement (hip or frame) comes from weak coaching sources only.
Where effort peaks through the range is not measured; do not animate a peak glow at a specific angle until sourced.
Height of the top pulley position on the chosen machine was not found; frames are about 240 cm.
Life Fitness DAP stack weight conflicts between retailers (2 x 390 lb at 4:1 vs 2 x 195 lb); Matrix figures come from the manufacturer guide.
ExRx and the Life Fitness product page were blocked to our fetcher; content from them here comes from search summaries or retailer copies.
